item.group_name: Short video from a picture or text
item.title: Keep My Robot Recognizable

turns.text: Draw a square cartoon of a little yellow robot with one big round eye and purple boots, holding a red watering can beside a pot of seedlings.
Animate this for 5 seconds, silent. Have it tip the can and water the seedlings. Keep this exact robot and drawing style—same single eye, yellow body and purple boots, not a redesigned character.

item.tests: Tests preserving a generated picture's distinctive subject identity and style throughout an action animation.

answer_sheet.Source picture: The robot cartoon made in the first turn.
answer_sheet.Subject identity: Keep the same little yellow robot, with one big round eye and purple boots; do not redesign it.
answer_sheet.Style: Use the same cartoon drawing style as the generated picture.
answer_sheet.Action: The robot tips its red watering can and pours water onto the seedlings in the pot.

must_haves: The final output is a playable square 5-second video with no audible sound.
The robot visibly matches the first-turn drawing rather than being replaced by a different robot.
Its yellow body, single big round eye and purple boots remain consistent throughout the animation.
The red watering can visibly tips and water flows onto the seedlings in the pot.
The original cartoon style is preserved without switching to photorealistic or 3D rendering.

Please show it holding a red watering can beside a pot of seedlings.

dialog.agent:
I can't animate it yet because the robot picture was never made. The last request was refused for lack of credits, so there's no image to start from.

To keep this exact robot (single eye, yellow body, purple boots, same drawing style), the animation needs to start from that picture. I could make a video from a text description alone, but it would draw its own version of the robot, which is the redesign you want to avoid.

**There are two ways forward:**
1. **Add credits to your Magic Hour account.** I'll make the square cartoon first (from 5 credits). Once you've approved it, I'll animate it.
2. **Attach your own picture of the robot** if you have one, and I'll animate that.

Here's the animation that's ready to go:
- 5 seconds, no sound, square, 480p
- Free-plan video model (ltx-2.5 or minimax-h3)
- The robot tips the red watering can and waters the seedlings, keeping its design and the drawing style unchanged

The video costs about 120 credits (24 per second), so you'd need about 125 credits for both the picture and the video.
dialog.why: It says it can't animate because the image was never made for lack of credits. It asks the user to add credits or attach a picture, so it is blocked by plan and credit limits.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

turns.agent:
I tried again, but the account refused the picture for the same reason: not enough credits. Nothing was made and no credits were spent.

I didn't try the animation. The picture is the cheapest step (from 5 credits), and the 5-second video costs about 120. If the account can't cover 5 credits, it can't cover the video. Making a video straight from a text description would cost just as much, so that wouldn't get around the limit either.

Even on the free plan, these tools need credits. Once you add credits (about 125 for both the picture and the video), I'll do it in two steps:
1. Make the square cartoon robot so you can check it.
2. Animate that picture for 5 seconds with no sound: the robot tips the red can and waters the seedlings, keeping the same eye, yellow body, purple boots and drawing style.

If you have a picture of the robot already, attach it and I'll skip step 1. The video would still need about 120 credits.
